comment: Trigger globs for the heavy suites CI's `Test` job pays for (ADR 0140). `Setup Affected Context` resolves this against a pull request's changed paths with tools/scripts/ci/resolve-gate-triggers.ts and outputs one `run_<suite>` flag per entry; each suite's step runs when its flag is set, and unconditionally on a push. A change to any `sharedInputs` glob sets every flag, and so does a resolver error — the fallback is always to run more, never less. `id` is the gate name a review obligation's `coveringGate` spells (ADR 0098), which is what `yarn covering-gates:check` matches on: a path-gated Covering Gate whose triggers do not cover an obligation's trigger paths fails that check, because a reviewer must never suppress a finding on the strength of a gate the path gate skipped (ADR 0074). Add a heavy suite here, not an `if:` expression written by hand in the workflow.

suites.why: Every Contract Suite under tools/scripts in one `node --test` run (ADR 0135) — the checker contracts, the review pipeline, the release and staging deploy contracts, and the sandcastle decisions. The triggers are every tree those suites compile or read from the real repository, not just tools/ itself: the Husky hooks and workflow files whose wiring several suites assert, the composite action tools/scripts/lib/review-tier-workflow.test.ts and tools/scripts/review/run-facts-wiring.test.ts read, the skills and agent bodies they import, the sandcastle inputs tools/scripts/lib/sandcastle-cli-version.test.ts reads, the deployment pages tools/scripts/check-deploy-pipeline.test.ts copies, and the brand sources tools/scripts/generate-brand-logos.test.ts, check-web-app-icons.test.ts and check-mobile-app-icon.test.ts read — the brand-logo suite is the only thing in the tree that asserts those token names, since its generator is reached by no gate. A suite proves its checker works, and the checker itself still runs over the whole tree on every pull request through `yarn gates:run`; what this list must not omit is a tree a suite reads with no checker standing behind it.

suites.ciStep: Upstream Brief report contract and checker contracts
suites.why: The report contract, renderer, CLIs, and ledger suites that ship beside the upstream-brief Skill rather than under tools/scripts, so `tools:test`'s glob does not reach them (ADR 0084). Triggered by the Skill directory they live in and the adapter config they read.

suites.ciStep: Check OpenAPI spec and generated client are in sync
suites.why: Regenerates the TSOA spec and the generated client, then asserts a clean tree — the Covering Gate for the generated API surface (ADR 0074's worked example, issue #408). The triggers are every input of the chain `api-specs:sync` runs: `apps/backend/**` rather than `apps/backend/src/**`, because `apps/backend/tsoa.json` is the generator config itself and holds the servers, securityDefinitions, specVersion and controller globs the spec is built from; then the sync script that rewrites the spec into libs/api-specs, the spec project, the generated client, and the generator config. `package.json` is a shared input, which is how a release version bump — the change that originally left the client stale — still runs it.

The one TypeScript program no Nx project owns. ADR 0141 moves typecheck onto a per-project Inferred Target, so `nx affected -t typecheck` selects the projects a pull request can reach and the Nx computation cache covers the rest — but `tools/scripts` has no `project.json` on purpose (ADR 0135), and the plugin keys inference on `project.json`, so the `scripts` node Nx infers there from its `package.json` carries no `typecheck` target and `run-many` cannot reach its config. It stays the fixed job `check-typecheck.ts` runs, and this is what bounds it: the triggers are the tree that program compiles, which is not only tools/scripts. `include: ["**/*.ts"]` is rooted there, and `allowJs` pulls in the `.mjs` files beside it — `.agents/skills/upstream-brief/*.mjs`, which type the imports in `check-upstream-briefs.ts` and `copilot-hooks/upstream-brief-suggestion.ts` (ADR 0135 leaves those files out of the migration). Neither `tools:test` nor `upstream:briefs:test` type-checks anything, since `node --test` strips types, so dropping an export from one of them would otherwise reach `main` unchecked. The program does not extend `tsconfig.base.json`, so nothing outside those two trees changes its meaning except the TypeScript version, which `yarn.lock` and `package.json` already carry as shared inputs.

suites.ciStep: Apply Prisma migrations and check schema drift
suites.why: Tier 2 of the Prisma migration gate (ADR 0094): applies the migration history to an ephemeral Postgres and asserts applying it reproduces the schema. Unlike the other suites here it carries its own job rather than a step in `Test`, so a pull request that cannot have broken a migration never pays for the Postgres service start (ADR 0140, issue #1394). The triggers are the schema and migrations a changed path could actually drift: the Prisma schema directory, including its migrations, and the config file `migrate diff --from-config-datasource` reads its datasource from. The job also runs the migration backfill test, which `Test` excludes because `Test` carries no database, so that test file and the backend Jest config it runs under are triggers too: a pull request editing only the test would otherwise run it nowhere.
